name: fenicsx-same-problem
title: PDE engine swap, FV (VCell FV_SOLVER scheme) vs FEniCSx Q1 under the same coupling
question:
Can the PDE half of the co-simulation be swapped for a different discretization
(FEniCSx, Q1 finite elements) without changing anything else, and does that change the
coupled result beyond discretization error?
hypothesis:
FenicsxReactionDiffusion exposes the same ports as FVReactionDiffusion. On a structured
mesh whose vertices are the grid nodes, its lumped mass equals the FV control volumes, so
particle binning and units are unchanged. Q1 and FV are both second order. On matched
grids, the coupled hybrid results should agree to within sampling.
objective:
Part 1: cosine-mode diffusion on N×N grids (N = 11 ... 81) for three engines (FV, Q1
lumped mass, Q1 consistent mass), each compared to the analytic decay; h-orders fitted.
Part 2: A4's A_p + B_f → C_f on the 11×11×3 slab, 16 seeds per engine with the same
seeds (common random numbers, so paired comparison); survival and produced C compared.
description:
The swap is one composite argument (build_hybrid_document(pde_engine="fenicsx")); the
SmoldynHybrid process, the coupling and the model are untouched. In VCell the PDE
discretization is part of the solver (vcell-fvsolver's FV scheme, or vcell-fenics as a
separate solver), rather than an interchangeable component of the hybrid coupling.

canonical_runs.name: default
canonical_runs.label: Cosine-mode h-convergence (3 engines) + coupled engine swap (16 paired seeds)

conclusion:
Results (results/metrics.json, 2026-10-03):
- **All three engines are second order:** h-orders 1.97 (FV), 1.98 (Q1 lumped) and
  2.04 (Q1 consistent).
- **Error at N = 81:** 5.5e-6 (FV), 1.6e-5 (lumped) and 4.7e-6 (consistent).
- **Coupled, the swap changes nothing measurable:**
  - paired |z| = 1.50 (lumped) and 0.76 (consistent) against FV;
  - mean survival differences of 3·10⁻⁴ and 1·10⁻⁴;
  - all three within 0.27% of the continuum.
The PDE engine is interchangeable under the co-simulation, and discretization effects
are cleanly separable from coupling effects.
